references.text: In [ref:Joh 20:19|John 20:19], Jesus comes and stands among the disciples while the doors are locked, saying, "Peace be with you!" — a direct parallel account to Jesus' sudden appearance among them after the resurrection.
[ref:Joh 20:26|John 20:26] describes another occasion where Jesus again stands among the disciples and greets them with peace, confirming the pattern of his sudden appearances after the resurrection.
In [ref:Mark 16:14|Mark 16:14], Jesus reveals himself to the eleven while they are eating, a parallel account to the same event where the risen Christ appears to the disciples.
[ref:1 Kor 15:5|1 Corinthians 15:5] testifies that Christ appeared to Cephas and then to the twelve, confirming the historical testimonies of Jesus' appearances after the resurrection.

Earlier in the same chapter, in [ref:Luk 24:15|Luke 24:15], Jesus draws near and walks with the travelers on the road to Emmaus without them recognizing him — a similar pattern where the risen Jesus is suddenly present among his own.

[ref:Jes 9:5-6|Isaiah 9:5–6] prophesies about the Prince of Peace who is to come. Jesus, standing here among the disciples after his resurrection, is the fulfillment of this promise of peace and eternal dominion.

In [ref:Joh 14:27|John 14:27], Jesus promises, "Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you." His appearance among the disciples after the resurrection is a concrete fulfillment of this promise of peace.
[ref:Luk 24:37|Luke 24:37] is the immediate continuation where the disciples are terrified and frightened, thinking they see a spirit — this shows the effect of Jesus' sudden appearance among them.
